items.headline: Rząd bierze się za zamrożenie cen gazu na 2027 rok
items.summary: projekt przewiduje maksymalną cenę 197,29 zł/MWh dla gospodarstw domowych i odbiorców chronionych, czyli tyle samo co w tym roku.
items.matters: koszt to ponad 6 mld zł, a pokryć ma go nowy podatek od największych importerów.
items.body: Skomentuj Od 1 stycznia do 31 grudnia 2027 r. maksymalna cena gazu m.in. dla gospodarstw domowych ma wynieść 197,29 zł/MWh, czyli tyle ile w tym roku - wynika z projektu ustawy w tej sprawie. Według resortu energii bez tych rozwiązań gospodarstwa domowe zapłaciłby za gaz od 77 zł do ponad 1,8 tys. zł więcej. fot. Aristal / / Pixabay W piątek na stronach Rządowego Centrum Legislacji opublikowano projekt ustawy o szczególnej ochronie niektórych odbiorców paliw gazowych w 2027 r. w związku z sytuacją na rynku gazu oraz o zmianie niektórych ustaw. Został on przygotowany przez resort energii. Projektowane przepisy zakładają, że w okresie od 1 stycznia do 31 grudnia 2027 r. obowiązywać będzie maksymalna cena gazu dla odbiorców chronionych, w tym gospodarstw domowych. Dotyczyć to będzie również wspólnot i spółdzielni mieszkaniowych, a także podmiotów realizujących ważne zadania z zakresu użyteczności publicznej takie jak np. szkoły, szpitale, domów opieki, kościoły, noclegownie. Zgodnie z projektem sprzedawcy gazu w rozliczeniach z wyżej wymienionymi odbiorcami końcowymi będą stosowali cenę maksymalną wynoszącą 197,29 zł/MWh. Cena ta nie nie zawiera podatku VAT oraz podatku akcyzowego. „Poziom tej ceny odpowiada poziomowi ceny paliw gazowych w taryfie przedsiębiorstwa energetycznego będącego sprzedawcą z urzędu ustaloną na poziomie 197,29 zł/MWh i obowiązującą do końca 2026 r. (...)” - wskazano w uzasadnieniu projektu. Minister energii Miłosz Motyka powiedział w piątek wieczorem na antenie Polsat News, że liczy na to, iż projekt trafi pod obrady Sejmu w listopadzie, tak by do końca roku ustawa w tej sprawie mogła trafić na biurko prezydenta. „Ustalenie maksymalnej ceny paliw gazowych na poziomie określonym w ustawie ograniczy wpływ wzrostu cen rynkowych na wysokość rachunków ponoszonych przez odbiorców objętych ochroną w 2027 r. Zgodnie z przyjętymi w projekcie ustawy założeniami, gospodarstwa domowe oszczędzą średnio w skali roku od 77 zł (w przypadku tzw. kuchenkowiczów) do 1863 zł (w przypadku gospodarstw domowych wykorzystujących paliw gazowych do celów grzewczych)” - wskazano w ocenie skutków regulacji dołączonej do projektu ustawy. W projekcie utrzymuje się wprowadzony ustawą z 26 stycznia 2022 r. mechanizm składania oświadczeń przez odbiorców (np. spółdzielnie mieszkaniowe) przedsiębiorcom energetycznym dostarczającym gaz i które będą stanowiły podstawę do objęcia ich mechanizmem ochronnym. Gospodarstwa domowe takich oświadczeń nie będą musiały składać. Nowe przepisy przewidują wprowadzenie mechanizmu ograniczenia nadzwyczajnych zysków, które to mają…

items.headline: MSWiA szykuje się na nawet 2,5 mln uchodźców
items.summary: według "Rzeczpospolitej" resort analizuje trzy scenariusze, w tym masowy exodus z Kijowa i Odessy przed najtrudniejszą zimą wojny.
items.matters: z punktów recepcyjnych z 2022 roku zostały tylko dwa, w Przemyślu i Lublinie.
items.body: 17 listopada 2026, 07:26 28 komentarzy Udostępnij Udostępnij na Facebooku Udostępnij na X Udostępnij na WhatsApp Kopiuj link Nawet 2,5 mln uchodźców przed zimą. Polsce grozi fala uchodźców Źródło zdjęć: © East News | Andrzej Iwanczuk/REPORTER Rosja celowo niszczy ukraińską infrastrukturę energetyczną, by wywołać katastrofę humanitarną. Najbliższa zima może być najtrudniejsza od początku wojny, a do Polski może trafić nawet 2,5 mln uchodźców. MSWiA analizuje trzy scenariusze i przygotowuje się do kryzysu – pisze we wtorek "Rzeczpospolita". Zbliżająca się zima może być najtrudniejszą od wybuchu wojny. Jak donosi wtorkowa "Rzeczpospolita", celowe niszczenie ukraińskich linii przesyłowych przez Rosję ma doprowadzić do blackoutu państwa i katastrofy humanitarnej . Krzysztof Nieczypor z Ośrodka Studiów Wschodnich ocenia, że ataki na sieci cieplne, energetyczne oraz wodociągi mogą uniemożliwić codzienne życie w dużych miastach. DLA CIEBIE "Oddaliśmy tej dziczy flagę". Ostre wystąpienie działacza lewicy Ewentualny exodus ludności miejskiej może okazać się większy niż fala uchodźców z początku rosyjskiej inwazji . "Rz" przywołuje opinię podpułkownika Macieja Korowaja, byłego oficera Służby Wywiadu Wojskowego. Z szacunków wynika, że tylko z Kijowa i Odessy, liczących łącznie około 4,5 mln mieszkańców, do Polski mogłoby przyjechać nawet 2,5 mln osób. Ministerstwo Spraw Wewnętrznych i Administracji analizuje obecnie trzy scenariusze rozwoju sytuacji: brak napływu uchodźców, migrację osób planujących dołączyć do rodzin przebywających już w Polsce oraz masowy exodus. Resort deklaruje gotowość na ten ostatni, najtrudniejszy wariant, choć oficjalnie uznawany jest on obecnie za najmniej prawdopodobny. – Najbardziej prawdopodobny jest przyjazd Ukraińców mających w Polsce rodziny – ocenił cytowany przez gazetę wiceszef MSWiA Maciej Duszczyk. Zmasowany cios Ukrainy. 800 dronów nad Moskwą Polityk przyznał, że administracja odnotowuje już sygnały od obywateli Ukrainy. – Pojawiają się już pojedyncze pytania o możliwość schronienia się w Polsce na zimę – poinformował wiceminister. Zaznaczył jednak, że służby kontrolują sytuację. Nie ma obecnie sytuacji alarmowej – uspokoił Duszczyk. Administracja państwowa podjęła już pierwsze kroki zapobiegawcze. Wojewodowie przeprowadzili inwentaryzację dostępnej infrastruktury i zasobów, a Straż Graniczna na bieżąco monitoruje sytuację na przejściach. "Rzeczpospolita" przypomina jednocześnie, że Polska zlikwidowała większość punktów recepcyjnych i miejsc masowego zakwaterowania utworzonych w 2022 r. Obecnie funkcjonują tylko dwie takie…

items.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO tomorrow
items.summary: 825 million shares at $70–78, up to $64.4bn raised, trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under ANT.
items.matters: the biggest live test of whether AI valuations survive a chip-driven selloff.
items.body: Good morning. Anthropic set a proposed IPO valuation of up to roughly $1.4 trillion, below earlier reported expectations, but strong investor demand may already be pushing it higher. In an amended SEC filing on Tuesday, the Claude maker said it plans to offer 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 apiece in its proposed initial public offering. At the top of that range, the shares would have a combined value of approximately $64.35 billion. The offering includes shares sold by existing shareholders, from which Anthropic will receive no proceeds. Separately, Google, Nvidia , AMD , Broadcom , Micron , Microsoft and TSMC Partners, an affiliate of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, have agreed to purchase a combined $26 billion of Anthropic’s nonvoting Class N common stock through a private placement immediately following the IPO, according to the filing. That would bring the combined total to as much as $90.4 billion. Just weeks ago, reports had put the company’s potential valuation at roughly $2 trillion. Now, Anthropic’s bankers are considering pricing shares above the filed range, which could lift the valuation to $1.5 trillion or more, the Financial Times reported . Anthropic, which plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT, launched its roadshow on Tuesday, and the deal is expected to price on Nov. 18. CFO Krishna Rao , who joined Anthropic in 2024, is not selling any shares in the IPO. According to the filing, he beneficially owned about 9.5 million Class A shares as of Sept. 30, nearly all of it in stock options. At the top of the proposed range, that stake would have a gross value of roughly $740.8 million, before the cost of exercising the options and taxes. Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., wrote in a Tuesday note that the deal sets up a debate over “margin against growth,” with the stock likely to trade on whether Anthropic’s second-quarter operating profit or its third-quarter loss reflects its true run rate. Ives also argued that a more conservative valuation could help Anthropic achieve a successful market debut. The $1.4 trillion figure includes stock options and other equity awards. Counting only shares outstanding, he noted, the top of the range values the company at about $1 trillion. Andrew Murray was named CFO of Albertsons ( No.57 ), effective Jan. 17. Murray succeeds Cody Perdue, who has served as interim CFO since Sept. 30 and will continue as SVP of treasury, investor relations and risk management. Murray joins Albertsons from Fonterra Co-operative Group, the world's largest…

items.body: The newest iteration of the Qwen artificial intelligence series is now available through an API designed for professional workflows in sectors including manufacturing, finance, and scientific discovery. The model, Qwen4-Max, uses a mixture-of-experts architecture and features native vision and a 1M token context window, which the company says reduced the average cost per task by over 60% in internal tests compared to the previous Qwen3.8-Max. The model ranks in the top five on both the Spreadsheet and Python-PPTX arena leaderboards, which puts it in the same performance bracket as current flagship models from OpenAI and Anthropic. items.headline: Nvidia's Vera Rubin swept MLPerf Training v6.1 in its debut
items.summary: every benchmark led, and Nvidia also announced Rubin HPC with more than 50,000 CUDA cores on a single GPU.
items.matters: the roadmap keeps shipping while the board searches for a chief executive.
items.body: AI news today, November 17, 2026: Trump said he is open to Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia, while the board denied it is considering a comeback. The US tightened AI chip export rules, and the IMF warned that AI circular financing has topped $1 trillion. Here are the 10 top stories and 5 security stories, each with free, non-paywalled sources. President Donald Trump said he is open to Jensen Huang returning as Nvidia's CEO, telling reporters he "would certainly not mind seeing that." Trump said "a big group of people" wants Huang back, after a petition with more than 165,000 signatures called for his reinstatement. Nvidia's board is not considering a comeback, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. Directors are focused on a Wachtell Lipton investigation into Huang's conduct and national security risks, and the board is still selecting a search firm. Nvidia shares opened down 2.7% . The November 16 briefing covered Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's call for an outside CEO and the growing political pressure on the board. Why it matters: Trump's support gives Huang's allies a powerful voice, but the board's denial shows the investigation still controls the timetable. The Commerce Department issued an interim rule requiring licenses to export, reexport or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers abroad. The rule applies if they may provide compute to China or other restricted countries. It targets China, Russia, Iran, North Korea and 18 others. It applies to data centers or networks that can supply more than 12 million total processing performance, roughly 750 Nvidia H100 or H200 chips. New licenses are also required for Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil. Existing operators have 90 days to comply. Why it matters: The rule closes the overseas-compute loophole that Megaspeed allegedly used, and it turns export controls into a global licensing regime. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said the world economy is "standing on one leg" on AI, warning that a wobble could cause financial stability troubles. The IMF estimates circular financing among AI companies has grown to just over $1 trillion , about two-thirds of it debt-funded. Georgieva said the sum is "not a huge size, but it is a rapid increase." Nvidia has lost more than $1 trillion in market value over the past month. The IMF still expects 3.1% global growth this year, but it has warned that an AI disappointment could trigger a disorderly correction. Why it matters: AI investment is now a main engine of global growth, so a financing pullback would hit markets well…

items.headline: Microsoft put a 138bn-parameter coding model on local GPUs
items.summary: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash ships a 53 GiB mixed-precision checkpoint through Foundry and runs as the local model in GitHub Copilot.
items.matters: agentic coding is moving on-device, where export rules cannot reach it.
items.body: Monday's digest leads with the number that will be argued about all week: three days. Anthropic told IPO investors that its model did the software work to run on AMD GPUs in three days instead of six to 12 months. NVIDIA's next platform swept every MLPerf training benchmark in its debut and posted a tenfold gain in agentic tokens per watt. Google made a plain-language coder generally available inside Apps Script, Microsoft shipped a 138-billion-parameter coding model that runs on a local GPU, and three funding rounds in one day mapped where capital thinks the next moat sits: defense, self-improvement, and European deep tech. 1. Anthropic says Claude Mythos onboarded AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days Anthropic told IPO investors that its Claude Mythos Preview model did the software work required to run one of its AI models on AMD's MI355X GPUs in about three days, with basically no human intervention, and that the same job historically took six to 12 months with dozens of engineers. Tom Brown, Anthropic's co-founder and chief compute officer, made the comparison in a roadshow video dated November 10, and the amended prospectus filed the same day states that the company can onboard new chip platforms in a fraction of the time it once took. The slide footnote narrows the scope: the three days cover prompt processing for one model on MI355X at what Anthropic calls a useful level of performance, and Mythos ported or wrote almost 100 percent of the kernels. Kernels are the low-level programs that tie a model to a specific vendor's silicon, and writing them has been part of NVIDIA's CUDA moat for nearly two decades. AMD's equivalent stack is ROCm, with HIP as the programming layer and HIPify as the conversion tool, and AMD has spent a year arguing that AI can do this work: its researchers published the GEAK kernel-writing agent in August 2025, its AI software VP said in April that Claude beats HIPify because it has web search built in, and its SVP of AI reported in July that AI-generated kernels were sometimes better than the most manually tuned versions. Anthropic runs its models on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, Google TPUs, and AWS Trainium, managed as one fungible pool of compute, and holds an agreement with AMD for up to 2 gigawatts. Its first MI450-based Helios racks are expected in the first half of 2027, which will test whether the three-day bring-up repeats on new silicon. The claim carries honest limits. The scope covers prefill for one model, decode is unaddressed, there is no speed comparison against NVIDIA hardware, and the six-to-12-month baseline is…

items.body: This observation covers AI technology changes formally released or reliably verified around the period from 7:53 am on 16 November to 7:53 am on 17 November 2026 in Australia/Sydney. It includes three items. Alibaba formally released Qwen4-Max on 16 November under the model identifier qwen4-max. It is callable through QwenCloud's Token Plan and API and is also available in QwenWork and QwenStudio. The Qwen4-Max-Preview opened on 11 November only through the Singapore Token Plan and is scheduled to end on 25 November; the new fact in this release is that a separate production model is now live. Alibaba describes it as a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 2.4 trillion total parameters and 71 billion activated per token. It natively accepts text, image and video input and provides a one-million-token context window, tool calling and structured output. The flagship model's weights have not been released; Alibaba has only announced plans for smaller open-weight Qwen4 models. Performance, cost, safety and long-running agent results are developer reports. Reuters did not independently verify them, and no complete public third-party reproduction is available. The US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security issued the interim final rule Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors on 16 November, and it took effect immediately. The rule adds section 744.24 to the Export Administration Regulations. A licence is required when an exporter knows that covered advanced-computing items will be used in a data centre anywhere in the world and that one or more linked data centres will provide more than 12,000,000 aggregate TPP of direct or indirect access to a company headquartered, or whose ultimate parent is headquartered, in Macau or Country Group D:5. Foreign data centres must examine direct and indirect customer ownership or control. Compute used exclusively for commercial recommender systems is excepted when reporting conditions are met. The rule also adds destination-based licence requirements for specified advanced-computing items sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. Existing remote services may continue for 90 days but must obtain a licence within that period. The rule is in force as an interim final rule; licence applications are reviewed case by case, and implementation and any later amendments remain incomplete. TensorWave announced on 16 November that it had signed a six-year contract to provide OpenAI with 457 MW of dedicated, single-tenant AI capacity across multiple data centres. The plan uses AMD Helios…

items.body: SANTA MONICA, CALIF. (NOV. 16, 2026) — Nominations for the 2027 Grammys ® were announced today, and topping the list of nominees are RAYE (11) , ROSALÍA (9) , Ella Langley (7) , Miranda Lambert (7) , Olivia Rodrigo (7) , Phoebe Bridgers (7) , Bruno Mars (6) , Leon Thomas (6) ,and Olivia Dean (6) . As the only peer-voted music award, Grammy ® award winners are selected by the Recording Academy ® 's Voting Members , a body of nearly 16,000 music makers who represent all genres and creative disciplines, including recording artists, songwriters, composers, producers, mixers, and engineers. The full list of 2027 Grammy Award nominations is here . "It's a privilege to congratulate all the incredible music creators recognized in this year's Grammy nominations," said Harvey Mason jr., Grammys CEO. "From first-time nominees to artists reaching career milestones, it's inspiring to see musicians at every stage of their careers represented. Together, they reflect the extraordinary diversity of genres, crafts and backgrounds that make up our community. We look forward to a remarkable season of celebration, and I'm grateful to our Voting Members for their continued commitment to honoring the music that moves us year after year." This year's eligibility period includes recordings released from Aug. 31, 2025, through Aug. 28, 2026. Final Round Voting, in which Recording Academy Voting Members choose the Grammy winners, will take place Dec. 10, 2026 – Jan. 7, 2027. In a historic shift, the 2027 Grammys will return to ABC for the first time since 1972. The ceremony will premiere live across ABC, Disney+ and Hulu from Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Sunday, Feb. 7, 2027, at 7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT. The Telecast will be produced by Fulwell Entertainment for the Recording Academy, with Ben Winston, Raj Kapoor and Jesse Collins serving as executive producers. Earlier that day, the Grammy Awards Premiere Ceremony ® will stream live on Disney+ at 2:30 p.m. ET / 11:30 a.m. PT. Produced by Fulwell Entertainment, the ceremony will be executive produced by Winston, Eric Pankowski and Greg V. Fera. Branden Chapman, Chantel Sausedo, Rex Supa, and Ruby Marchand will serve as producers on behalf of the Recording Academy. It will take place at Peacock Theater. items.body: Helsinki's THE 69 EYES will release Acustica , an album of acoustic reworkings of their songs, on February 5, 2027 via BLKIIBLK. Alongside the announcement, the band has shared the second preview, a stripped-down "Wasting The Dawn (Forma Acustica)" with an official music video. "Wasting The Dawn" is one of the band's signature songs. As the title track of their 1999 album, it was THE 69 EYES' first international release through Roadrunner Records, and it has stayed in the live set ever since. The new version leans toward the cinematic sweep of Ennio Morricone's film scores while keeping the original's gothic atmosphere, and the band promises a glimpse of Jim Morrison's shadow somewhere in the video. The track was mixed by Matt Hyde, who produced the band's 2009 album Back In Blood and has worked with SLAYER and on MEGADETH's latest album. "Mystery is a great element in life," says singer Jyrki 69. "Sometimes you manage to capture it in art. That is what 'Wasting The Dawn' is all about. It is a spiritual song celebrating the youth." The acoustic campaign began in September with "Brandon Lee (Forma Acustica)", which also opens the album. The ten-track set revisits material from across the catalog, including the 2005 hit "Lost Boys", whose video was directed by Bam Margera. Formed in Helsinki in 1989, the "Helsinki Vampires" still play with their original lineup and have thirteen studio albums behind them, several of them gold and platinum in Finland. Earlier this year they released the I Survive EP, featuring a THIN LIZZY cover . Our archive also holds an interview with the band from 2008 . THE 69 EYES are: Jyrki 69 (vocals), Bazie (guitar, backing vocals), Timo-Timo (guitar), Archzie (bass, backing vocals), Jussi 69…

items.body: Nearly 1,000 high-level policymakers, start-ups, industry leaders and researchers will take part in the Apply AI Summit in Brussels tomorrow. They will discuss how artificial intelligence (AI) can boost Europe’s competitiveness across 10 strategic sectors and the public sector. The summit will also showcase concrete AI applications, European success stories and innovative projects. Henna Virkkunen , Executive Vice-President for Technological Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, will host the summit and present the first Apply AI Startup Award to three European start-ups. The award recognises innovative European startups and scaleups developing AI solutions in the strategic sectors. Alongside the in-person event, an online conference platform will run from 16 to 20 November, allowing additional 2,500 participants to join part of the summit. The Apply AI Summit marks one year since the adoption of the Apply AI Strategy , which sets out how to speed up the use of AI in Europe’s key industries and the public sector. items.headline: The Digital Fairness Act proposal would regulate design, not just disclosure

items.matters: subscription and checkout code becomes compliance code, and the Commission gets direct enforcement powers.
items.body: Had trouble with an online purchase or subscription lately? It’s an increasingly common phenomenon. According to the 2025 Consumer Conditions Scoreboard around 60% of us buy goods or services online, yet online shoppers are over 60% more likely to experience problems than those shopping offline. The European Commission’s newly proposed Digital Fairness Act will help ensure that whether you shop online or in a physical store, you will be guaranteed the same high level of consumer protection. The Act tackles unfair commercial practices online, such as manipulative marketing tactics or hidden fees, that undermine our ability to make free and informed choices. For, while online shopping is convenient, it shouldn’t come at the expense of fairness. The Act will protect consumers of all ages shopping and browsing for goods or services online. It will also mean fairer competition for businesses, which are expecting to save EU consumers up to €13.7 billion a year. The Digital Fairness Act proposal will also simplify the application of the Consumer Rights Directive online. For instance, by introducing simpler pre-contractual information requirements for repeat in-app purchases and clearer rules on how consumers can cancel digital media subscriptions within the withdrawal period.
